summary: Byambyn Rinchen was a scholar in linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Tibetology. He studied at the Leningrad Orient Institute (~1924–1927) and Eötvös Loránd University (~1956–1957), and later held a post at the National University of Mongolia.
Byung-gon Kim is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied abroad at Rissho University (attested 2007). He held a post as professor, dean, and institute director at Minobusan University (attested 2026).

C. C. Berg worked in linguistics, Indology, and history and archaeology. He studied at Leiden University in 1919 and completed his doctorate there (~1923–1927) under G. A. J. Hazeu and Nicolaas Johannes Krom, later serving as Professor of Javanese (1929–1972).

C. Collin Davies worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He earned a B.A. from Aberystwyth University (~1919–1922) and a Ph.D. from Peterhouse (~1922–1926), later serving as Lecturer at SOAS (1926–1936) and Reader at Oxford (1936–1963).

C. D. Sebastian specializes in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned a PhD from Banaras Hindu University, studied under mentors including Paul Williams and Gavin D'Costa, and became Professor of Indian Philosophy at the Indian Institute of Technology Bombay (attested 2016).

C. Kunhan Raja was an Indologist and philosopher who earned a D.Phil. at Oxford under Arthur Anthony Macdonell. He served as the first University Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Madras (1927) and directed the Adyar Library and Research Centre (1928–1938).
C. M. Naim worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at the University of California, Berkeley (~1957–1961) and served as Professor Emeritus at the University of Chicago (~2001–2025).

C. M. Ridding worked in Indology and Buddhist studies, studying at Girton College and Cambridge (M.A. ~1922–1923) under Edward Byles Cowell and T. W. Rhys Davids. She catalogued at Girton (1904) and served as Librarian at Cambridge University Library (1911).
C. Peter Bankart worked in Buddhist studies and related fields. He held an appointment at Wabash College (attested 2003) and served as a Visiting Researcher at Dartmouth College.

C. Pierce Salguero is a scholar of Buddhist studies and history, holding degrees from the University of Virginia and a Ph.D. from Johns Hopkins University. He became professor of Asian History and Health Humanities at Pennsylvania State University in 2010.
C. R. Krishnamacharlu worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Madras Christian College and Pachaiyappa's College, and served at the Archaeological Survey of India (~1911–1943).
C. S. Srinivasachariar was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He held professorships at Pachaiyappa's College and Annamalai University (attested 1932–1933).

C. W. Huntington, Jr. specialized in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Michigan (~1980–1986) under Luis Oscar Gómez and Madhav M. Deshpande, later serving as Professor at Hartwick College (~1992–2020).
Caixi Chen is a scholar of Buddhist studies who pursued a PhD at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies under the supervision of Wadinagala Pannaloka (attested 2026).

Calambur Sivaramamurti worked in Indology and archaeology, studying at Presidency University under S. Kuppuswami Sastri. He held posts at the Government Museum in Chennai (1935–1946), the Indian Museum, and the Archaeological Survey of India (~1946–1955).

Calvert Watkins worked in linguistics and Indology, earning his undergraduate degree and Ph.D. at Harvard under Joshua Whatmough. He served as professor of linguistics and classics at Harvard (1959–2003) and later as distinguished professor at UCLA (2003–2013).

Calvin Thomas worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at the University of Michigan (A.B. ~1870–1874) and the University of Leipzig (1877–1878), and held appointments at Michigan (1879–1896) and Columbia University (1896–1919).

Cameron Bailey specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Bailey completed undergraduate studies at Indiana University Bloomington under Richard F. Nance, an MA at Florida State University under Bryan J. Cuevas, and doctoral work at the University of Oxford under Ulrike Roesler.
Cameron David Warner is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under Yudru Tsomu. Warner has held academic posts at Dickinson College, Middlebury College, and Aarhus University.

Cameron Foltz works in religious studies and Japanology, earning an MA from Florida State University (attested 2018) under Bryan J. Cuevas. In 2025, Foltz held a postdoctoral fellowship at Columbia University's Weatherhead East Asian Institute.
